name: HubSpot

steps.d: Install the HubSpot CLI, run hs project create and choose App. Pick the distribution and OAuth when it asks.
In app-hsmeta.json, add your redirect URLs and list the scopes under requiredScopes.
Run hs project upload to send it to your HubSpot account.
On the project details page, open the app's Auth tab and copy the Client ID and Client secret into your OAuth server.

steps.t: Test in a developer test account
steps.d: Install the app in a developer test account first. Installers see an unverified-app warning until it's listed.

blockers.s: A Marketplace listing needs at least three active, unique installs.
Until a listing is approved, installers must authorize installing an unverified app.

agent: Choose the scopes your app needs
you: Run the CLI and upload the project
Submit a Marketplace listing, if you want one
sources: Create a new app using the CLI
diffReason: Moderate: apps work without review, but installers must accept an unverified-app warning until HubSpot's team approves a Marketplace listing

checklist.answer: Run hs project create in the HubSpot CLI and choose App when it asks for the project contents.
Choose whether to distribute on the HubSpot Marketplace or restrict installs to specific accounts. Use OAuth for many accounts, or a static token for one.
The app-hsmeta.json file sets the app's uid, name, description, distribution, auth and support details.
Add one or more valid redirect URLs to the app-hsmeta.json file. HubSpot's example uses a localhost URL for development.
Open your project's details page, click the Auth tab and copy the Client ID and Client secret from Client credentials.
List scopes under requiredScopes, and optionally under optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes.
Marketplace listing submissions are reviewed manually by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and rejected if they don't meet the criteria.
“Once you submit your listing, the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.”
You can test in a developer test account. Until the app is verified, anyone installing it must tick a box authorizing an unverified app.
Listings are rejected if they don't meet the criteria, which include using OAuth as the only authorization method and requesting only the scopes your app needs.
